title: Maximize Alternating Sum Using Swaps
summary: Given an integer array nums and a 2D integer array swaps where swaps[i] = [pi, qi], you can swap the elements at indices pi and qi any number of times to maximize the alternating sum of nums.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a 2D integer array swaps where swaps[i] = [pi, qi], you can swap the elements at indices pi and qi any number of times to maximize the alternating sum of nums. The alternating sum is calculated as the sum of elements at even indices minus the sum of elements at odd indices, i.e., nums[0] - nums[1] + nums[2] - nums[3].... Return the maximum possible alternating sum after performing the allowed swaps.
constraints: nums has two to 100,000 positive integers.
Each allowed index pair may be swapped any number of times and in any order.
Maximize the sum at even indices minus the sum at odd indices.
hints: Unlimited swaps along graph edges permit any permutation inside each connected component.
For each component, place its largest values in positive even-index slots and its smallest values in negative odd-index slots.
Use union-find to build components, sort their values, and sum the largest positive-slot count minus the rest.
An exchange argument shows that assigning a larger value to a positive slot never hurts; components are independent, so their optima add.
editorial: An exchange argument shows that assigning a larger value to a positive slot never hurts; components are independent, so their optima add.

tests.explanation: All indices connect, so place the two largest values at even indices for a maximum of four.
Only indices one and two exchange; keeping the original order gives the maximum two.
